insight: Only a trace of rain has fallen recently (1.8 mm) — very little rain, and too little to drive meaningful runoff. The model's main signals right now: high tide timing is raising risk — how long before mid-morning the last high tide fell, which sets how much the water has just washed off the upper beach; high tide level is raising risk — a high tide can mobilize bacteria held in wet sand and push the waterline toward outfalls; and seasonal pattern is raising risk — seasonal patterns (wet winters vs dry summers) set the baseline risk. The most recent sample, 5 days ago, was excellent at 20 MPN/100mL. It's a naturally clean, well-flushed open-coast beach (unsafe only ~3% of the time), so outside of storms it's reliably safe.
